title: Interactive Streaming LLM Service Contract Module — Data Minimization & Live Redaction Procedures
content:
Purpose and scope:
This contract module is intended to be appended to standard vendor/processor agreements where the vendor provides an interactive, streaming LLM inference service (including websockets/HTTP chunked responses, server-sent events, or equivalent). It defines obligations and operational controls for live redaction, data minimization, ephemeral telemetry, and testable audit evidence.

Applicability:
- Applies where Customer data (including PII, personal data, or regulated content) may be present in streaming inference requests or intermediate outputs (partial tokens, streaming segments, or on-the-fly function call payloads).
- Complements (does not replace) the main DPA and security exhibits; in case of conflict, the strictest obligation applies.

Key definitions (for contract clarity):
- Streaming Session: a single end-to-end logical interaction in which the vendor returns partial or incremental model outputs to the customer or end-user in real time.
- Live Redaction Hook: an API or runtime mechanism provided by the vendor that allows synchronous or near-synchronous removal or masking of identified sensitive content before it is sent to the customer or persisted.
- Ephemeral Telemetry: runtime traces and logs that exist for troubleshooting only and are retained only for the minimum period required for diagnosis unless explicitly escalated.
- Partial Token Data: any fragment of model output transmitted before finalization (including token-by-token streams, segments, or produced function arguments).

Contractual obligations (vendor responsibilities):
1) Data minimization by default:
   - Vendor shall implement default request-level handling that strips or redacts sensitive metadata fields (e.g., identity tokens, SSNs) from request headers/body before retention.
   - Vendor shall provide an allowlist approach for fields that may be retained for analytics; retention requires explicit Customer consent via configuration.

2) Live redaction capability and SLAs:
   - Vendor shall expose one or more Live Redaction Hooks callable inline with streaming sessions (synchronous or asynchronous with maximum processing latency).
   - SLA: For synchronous hooks, the vendor guarantees median redaction latency <= 60ms and 99th percentile <= 250ms for payloads <= 8KB under normal load profiles; exceptions must be documented in an annex.
   - Live redaction must support pattern-based rules, named entity detection, custom customer regex lists, and a fallback safe-mask option.

3) No unintended persistence of partial outputs:
   - Vendor must treat Partial Token Data as transient by default. Partial outputs should not be persisted to durable storage, logs, or analytics pipelines unless explicitly configured by the Customer.
   - If partial outputs are buffered for operational reasons, they must be encrypted in-transit and at-rest and automatically purged within a configurable short window (default <= 5 minutes).

4) Ephemeral telemetry & troubleshooting exception process:
   - Ephemeral Telemetry shall be limited to data essential for diagnosing streaming failures (connection IDs, session metrics, error traces).
   - Default retention for Ephemeral Telemetry is 72 hours; any extension requires documented Customer approval, with a maximum extension of 90 days and an audit trail capturing the approver and reason.

5) Live redact evidence and auditability:
   - Vendor shall produce a machine-readable audit trail for each redaction decision associated with a streaming session, including timestamp, rule/engine id, matched pattern, and whether masking or dropping occurred.
   - Audit trails may not include the redacted material in cleartext. If evidence must show an original exemplar for legal reasons, it must be provided under an encrypted, time-bound, and logged escrow workflow.

6) Data subject requests (DSRs) and reverse redaction requests:
   - For DSRs where a Customer requests copies of their data that were transmitted via streaming sessions, Vendor shall provide an export within 30 days in a machine-readable format, showing only data the Customer is contractually allowed to view (i.e., not other tenants’ data).
   - If reverse-redaction is requested (i.e., Customer requests the original unmasked content), Vendor shall require documented Customer proof of lawful basis and follow documented escrow retrieval procedures; such retrievals are auditable and limited.

7) Model caching and KV retention constraints:
   - Vendor shall document any prefix or KV caching behavior that may cause user-submitted tokens to be re-used in future sessions. Such cached artifacts must be scoped per-customer or per-session and cannot be used to train models or improve weights unless explicit opt-in is recorded.

8) Encryption, access controls, and key management:
   - All streams, hook calls, and auxiliary logs must use TLS 1.2+ and strong cipher suites.
   - Key management for any data-at-rest (including short-lived buffers) must support customer-provided keys (bring-your-own-key) where technically feasible.

9) Incident response specific to streaming inference data exposure:
   - Vendor must notify Customer within 24 hours of detection of any confirmed exposure of streaming session content outside intended recipients.
   - Notification must include scope (number of sessions affected), likely root cause, immediate mitigations, and suggested customer actions.

10) Penetration testing and proof-of-redaction exercises:
   - Vendor will allow an annual proof-of-redaction exercise under NDA: Customer may provide a curated test set (up to 500 streaming test sessions) to validate redaction performance. Vendor will provide summary metrics and anonymized examples of redactions.

Operational exhibits (to be attached):
- Exhibit A: Redaction Rule Specification (format, priority order, override rules).
- Exhibit B: Redaction Latency Measurement Methodology (how vendor measures latency for synchronous hooks).
- Exhibit C: Evidence Request Playbook (how Customer requests audit evidence and the workflow/delivery formats).
- Exhibit D: Cache Isolation Matrix (scoping of any prefix/KV caches by environment and tenant).

Sample clause language (pick-one insert block for downstream agreements):
"Live Redaction. Vendor shall operate Live Redaction Hooks for streaming sessions. Customer may supply rule-sets and custom entity lists; Vendor shall apply Customer-provided rules prior to delivering any partial or final output to the Customer or end-users. Vendor shall not persist unredacted Partial Token Data in durable logs, analytics, or model training artifacts without explicit Customer configuration and documented consent. Vendor shall provide audit evidence of redactions as described in Exhibit C." 

Liability and remedies:
- For material breaches of the Live Redaction obligations that cause unauthorized disclosure of Customer streaming data, Customer may seek contractual remedies including first priority remediation, reimbursements for documented remediation costs, and termination rights where breach is not cured within 30 days of notice.

Negotiation notes and recommended business terms (internal):
- Customers will commonly request lower latency SLAs and longer DSR windows; negotiate telemetry retention as a configurable parameter on dedicated deployments.
- Offer managed proof-of-redaction as a professional service for large enterprise deals.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, support full BYOK and shorter default telemetry retention (24 hours).

Checklist for legal review before signature:
- Confirm Exhibits A–D are completed and specific to the deployment model (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Populate latency annex with expected traffic profile benchmarks.
- Confirm whether cached prefixes or KV stores will be used and ensure per-customer isolation is documented.
- Attach sample audit evidence export schema.

Appendix: Example audit export JSON schema (redacted example) — for internal use only:
{
  "session_id": "<uuid>",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T12:03:22Z",
  "redaction_events": [
    {"offset": 142, "rule_id": "cust-regex-ssn-01", "action": "mask"},
    {"offset": 210, "rule_id": "ner-creditcard", "action": "drop"}
  ]
}

Notes to negotiators:
- This module aims to balance product viability (low-latency streaming) with provable privacy controls. Expect technical tradeoffs: synchronous redaction increases tail latency and operational cost; offer asynchronous safe-mask fallback for very high throughput tiers.

Revision history:
- Draft 0.1 (2024-11-02) initial scoping and sample clauses.
- Draft 0.2 (2024-12-09) added SLA numbers and DSR workflow.
- Draft 0.3 (2025-02-12) incorporated cryptography/BYOK notes and audit export schema.

Open questions for legal/engineering alignment:
- Can runtime accept customer-provided regex lists without normalization to avoid ReDOS risks? (Engineering)
- What is the default safe-mask character set and tokenization approach for partial tokens? (Product/Runtime)
- For Dedicated installs, what changes are required to allow BYOK across streaming buffers? (Security/Infra)

End of module.
